evals.name: Trigger - Specify permission and state behavior
evals.prompt: Create a durable repository-local spec for invitation acceptance. Requirements define actor permissions and expiry, while retries and duplicate acceptance are easy to misread.
evals.expected_output: One focused, testable behavior spec with provenance, state transitions, edge cases, and a minimal discoverability route.
expectations: Grounds normative rules in requirements or accepted decisions
Keeps code and tests labeled as observed evidence
Derives normal, failure, and material edge assertions as a review probe
Does not leak architecture, feature planning, or implementation detail into the spec

evals.name: Workflow - Preserve a core code and spec conflict
evals.prompt: The canonical auth requirement says revoked tokens return 401, but current tests and code return 403. Repair the spec only if authority is clear and report the remaining mismatch.
evals.expected_output: A precise conflict classification with no silent normalization or implementation edits.
expectations: States both claims and their evidence
Does not treat passing tests as intended truth
Reports the concrete code or test follow-up without editing those files

evals.name: Rerun - Keep human-authored rationale stable
evals.prompt: Run harness-specs again with unchanged requirements and code after a human clarified rationale in the canonical spec.
evals.expected_output: A no-op that preserves the human clarification and stable anchors.
expectations: Produces no semantic or formatting-only diff
Does not recreate an intentionally removed optional section
Preserves repository terminology and human-authored rationale

evals.name: No trigger - Obvious CRUD implementation
evals.prompt: Add a conventional admin-only CRUD endpoint whose behavior is already explicit in the current API contract and tests.
evals.expected_output: harness-specs should not trigger or should make an evidence-backed no-op if explicitly invoked.
expectations: Does not duplicate the existing API contract
